laws.heading: Nandi County: no alcohol for under 18s
laws.rule: Nandi County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2014, s 32: no person may sell, supply or provide an alcoholic drink to a person under 18. The penalty is a fine of up to KES 150,000 (about A$1,639; A$1 = KES 91.49 (CBK rate KES 129.96 per USD, 29 Oct 2026, with RBA A$1 = USD 0.7040, 30 Oct 2026)) or up to 1 year in prison, or both. A seller has a defence if they asked to see an age document and believed on reasonable grounds that it was genuine. The Act also bars under-18s from the part of licensed premises where alcohol is made, stored, sold or consumed. A person under 18 found buying or drinking alcohol can be sent to compulsory counselling and rehabilitation (s 32).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to KES 150,000 (about A$1,639) or 1 year for the seller

laws.heading: Nandi County: where and when alcohol can be sold or drunk
laws.rule: Nandi County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2014, s 38 (breach of licence): except as the Act provides, no person may sell alcohol in a workplace, office, factory, public park, public recreational facility, public transport vehicle, public beach, sports stadium or public street, and no person may sell, buy or drink alcohol at a selling outlet after the hours for which the outlet is licensed. For selling without the right licence, a first offence carries a fine of up to KES 1,000,000 (about A$10,930) or up to 1 year in prison, or both. See the separately dated First Schedule extraction below; actual venue licences and later amendments still need confirmation.
laws.penalty_signal: Fines and imprisonment under the county Act

laws.rule: Nandi County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act 2014, Act 6: Section 26: a licensee may refuse entry and must expel a drunk/disorderly, violent or quarrelsome person; refusing to leave when properly requested is an offence. Sections 36-38 cover sale to an already intoxicated person, drunk-and-incapable or drunk-and-disorderly public conduct, and buying/consuming after the outlet’s licensed hours.

Nandi County Alcoholic Drinks Control Act 2014, Act 6: First Schedule: general retail on-licence Monday-Friday 17:00-23:00, weekends/public holidays 14:00-23:00; rural/suburban wines-and-spirits off-licence 17:00-20:30 daily; urban supermarket/franchised retail off-licence 10:00-20:30 daily. Hotel lodger/guest and club/nightclub licences have different conditions. These are the original published county schedule, not verified hours of a particular venue or a check of later amendments.
